relevance_note: The paper describes three affected members of one Chinese family with Blau syndrome, each carrying a NOD2 variant: "A heterozygous mutation C>T transversion in exon 4 was identified in each patient".
method_note: Narrative case report of one pedigree; rows written by hand via a small Python script and every span checked verbatim by script. Labels are the pedigree labels III:5 (proband), III:6 (brother) and II:5 (father). Out of scope / no rows: the four unaffected tested relatives ('four unaffected individuals'; 'No such mutation was found in unaffected members') are described only as a group without labels or individual facts; the mother is mentioned only as having noticed the proband's rash. Variant: only the protein change (R334W / p.R334W) and 'C>T ... in exon 4' are printed; no c. string or transcript (sequence compared with GenBank NG_007508.1, a genomic RefSeqGene, not recorded as transcript). Variant type 'missense' taken from the authors' wording 'amino acid substitution'. Zygosity from 'A heterozygous mutation ... was identified in each patient'. Inheritance for III:5 and III:6 recorded as 'inherited paternal' because their father II:5 is one of the patients stated to carry the same heterozygous mutation; the mother's testing status is not stated. Contradiction: the abstract says 'skin granulomas were found in all affected members', but the father II:5 was 'not manifested with exanthema' and had 'no manifestation of dermatitis'; both rows emitted for II:5 and his checklist item for skin rash is set to not reported. 'None of the patients had lung and other organs involvement' (named group: the three patients) was used to exclude lung involvement and hence interstitial lung disease; 'other organs involvement' was recorded as a feature row but not used to exclude specific checklist organs (hepatic, splenic, renal, cardiac) because it is non-specific. Normal chest X-ray recorded as 'abnormal chest X-ray' excluded (excludes nothing more specific). Negative ANA/ASO/RF/HLA-27/CRP and normal ESR recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27). III:6 visual acuity 20/25 OD not treated as impairment or its absence. The Discussion's comparison (proband had 'more severe anterior uveitis companied by glaucoma and cataract' than father and brother) was not used to exclude glaucoma or cataract in II:5 or III:6. PIP contracture/ankylosis in II:5 not mapped to camptodactyly. All patients were initially diagnosed with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (no age given), so age at diagnosis is not reported.
